title: Natural shifted Hom identification for restricted global RHom
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be any morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $P,Q\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. With global RHom [def-pc-global-derived-rhom] restricted along $\Gamma(S)\to\Gamma(X)$, for all integers $m,n$ there are additive equivalences $e_{P,Q,m,n}:H^{n-m}(RHom_X(P,Q))\simeq Hom(P[m],Q[n])$. For every $q:Q\to Q\prime$ and cohomology class $x$, $e_{P,Q\prime,m,n}(H^{n-m}(RHom_X(P,q))(x))=e_{P,Q,m,n}(x)\circ q[n]$. There are no boundedness or quasi-coherence hypotheses. Module and sheaf localization universes may be chosen independently.

proof.text: Compute internal RHom using a K-flat source and K-injective target. Apply the natural global RHom/derived Hom identification to the shifted representatives. Degree n-m cocycles modulo boundaries are maps P[m] to Q[n].

Exact scalar restriction leaves the underlying group unchanged and commutes with cohomology. Postcomposition with q commutes with the representative maps, shifts and localization, giving the asserted naturality.

theorem restrictedGlobalHom_shiftedHom_equiv
    [∀ Z : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ (R : Type u) [Ring R], HasDerivedCategory.{wA} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    ∃ e : ∀ (P Q : schemeDerivedCategory X) (m n : ℤ),
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))) (n - m)).obj
          ((schemeGlobalScalarRestriction f).obj
            ((schemeGlobalDerivedHom X).obj (op P, Q)))) ≃+ (P⟦m⟧ ⟶ Q⟦n⟧),
      ∀ (P Q Q' : schemeDerivedCategory X) (m n : ℤ) (q : Q ⟶ Q')
        (x : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))) (n - m)).obj
            ((schemeGlobalScalarRestriction f).obj
              ((schemeGlobalDerivedHom X).obj (op P, Q))))),
        e P Q' m n
          (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))) (n - m)).map
              ((schemeGlobalScalarRestriction f).map
                ((schemeGlobalDerivedHom X).map ((𝟙 P).op, q)))) x) =
          e P Q m n x ≫ q⟦n⟧'
